appropriate: the double rule under 'Clear Ledger' reads as the ledger's totalled sum with no caption; plain, level and Everyman, though 'see where you stand' is implied rather than shown
distinctive: no circle or tile like Xero or QuickBooks, and title case with a real word space sets it apart, but a CL monogram over a double underline is a generic silhouette any accountant could use
simple: one sentence: the name, or CL, set over a double rule; drawable in seconds, though the icon is two letters plus two rules rather than one shape
legible: the wordmark reads at a glance at 128 px and in the one-colour 64 panel; CL holds at 24 px, but at 16 px the letters are tiny and the two rules nearly merge
adaptable: the black, reversed and one-colour panels all hold, the moss app tile and tab favicon work unchanged, and the rules suggest a draw-on motion
timeless: a humanist sans in title case with a bookkeeper's double rule; no trend shape, would have read the same ten years ago
universal: the mirrored panel is only reversed text and the rotated panel reads clean; no secondary figure appears
clear: unsearched: CL monograms and double-underlined wordmarks are common among small accountancy and bookkeeping firms, and other 'Clear Ledger' firms already trade, so look-alikes are likely in the category
congruent: dark moss green, humanist sans in title case, two spaced words, level and symmetric, open frame, ruling as the category cue all match; the semibold weight sits slightly heavy for sincerity and the thin lower rule risks a hairline on the receipt printer
system: horizontal wordmark, CL symbol, app icon, favicon and the 256 to 16 ladder all derive from one rule; no stacked lockup is shown on the sheet
